questions.question: What does `[10, 20, 30, 40, 50][1:4]` return?
questions.explanation: List slicing `[start:end]` includes the element at index `start` and excludes `end`. Indices 1, 2, 3 hold the values 20, 30, 40. Index 4 (value 50) is excluded.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
```python
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
b.append(4)
print(a)
```
questions.explanation: `b = a` does NOT copy the list — both `a` and `b` point to the same list object in memory. When `b.append(4)` modifies the list, `a` sees the change too. To create an independent copy use `b = a.copy()` or `b = a[:]`.

questions.question: Which method adds a single element to the END of a list?
questions.explanation: `.append(item)` adds one item to the end of the list. `.extend(iterable)` adds all elements of an iterable. `.insert(index, item)` adds an item at a specific position. Lists have no `.add()` method (that belongs to sets).

questions.question: What does `sorted([3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9])` return?
questions.explanation: `sorted()` returns a NEW sorted list and does not modify the original. To sort a list in place, use `.sort()`. Note the difference: `sorted(my_list)` vs `my_list.sort()`.

questions.question: A data analyst has `prices = [10.5, 22.0, 8.75]`. Which expression gives the highest price?
questions.explanation: `max(prices)` returns the largest element without modifying the list. `prices[-1]` gives the last element (22.0 here, but only because the list happens to end there). `prices.sort()[0]` would fail because `.sort()` returns `None`.
